execution_notes: Per-test compile, elaboration, and simulation logs are preserved in each test subdirectory.
XSim runs used isolated temporary build directories under %TEMP%/riscforge_xsim_20261019_run02; Timer0 used %TEMP%/riscforge_xsim_20261019_timer0.

Timer0 required a staged compatibility testbench and source list because the checked-in filelist has stale references and the original bench has XSim-incompatible constructs. No RTL design file was edited.

Timer0's initial Z failure was caused by xelab --override_timeunit overriding the vendor flash model's 1 ps unit. With the override omitted, 300e6 model time units correctly represent 300 us, the flash is powered before boot read, and the staged smoke passes.

Timer0 final staged run commands, from its temporary RTL_SOC working directory: xvlog.bat --sv --nolog -d XSIM soc_timer0_boot_run_tb.sv; xelab.bat --nolog --timescale 1ns/1ps --debug all soc_timer0_boot_run_tb -s timer0_correct_timescale; xsim.bat timer0_correct_timescale -runall -nolog.
Timer0 staged testbench waits for both park PC and the committed DSRAM result; the checked-in testbench and RTL were not modified.

Monitor follow-up: rf_monitors.sv now constructs the packed LSU transaction atomically after the exact-path test exposed lost byte enables under XSim. The isolated smoke passes one-to-one LSU/AXI/APB UART payload/strobe matching; this is structural monitor-harness evidence, not Stage1 SoC accounting.
APB timeout follow-up: standalone test of the actual apb_timeout_monitor passes 14 checks under XSim 2022.2; source, filelist, compile/elab/simulation logs are preserved in monitor/apb_timeout_unit/.

Step4 checker self-proof was rerun from an isolated copy of the checker sources. The real-path bridge cannot be elaborated by XSim in this harness, so the checker test uses step4_apb_bridge_model; it is not real SoC timeout propagation evidence.

Step4 result: disassembler 31/31, clean non-vacuous traffic (LSU=17, AXI WR=8/RD=9, APB=14), injected fault matrix 11/11 expected IDs, runner GREEN. XSim warns that cover property statements are unsupported; this run does not claim functional coverage closure.

spi_master.checks: 26 pass indications, no fail indication; TC6 EOT timeout remains unresolved even though PREADY recovery and data check pass.

uart.checks: Compile and elaboration pass; XSim stops progressing after reset checks. Controlled benches show a no-time-advance stall on the APB-to-OBI combinational grant path; no-DUT control advances, minimal UART APB read and adapter-only apb_to_obi with synthetic gnt=req reproduce, forcing gnt low advances, and disabling OBI assertions does not fix it. This is not confirmed as an RTL defect or XSim bug.

soc_timer0_boot_runtime.root_cause_of_prior_failure: Elaboration option --override_timeunit overrode the S25FS512S model's 1 ps time unit. Its 300 us power-up delay became 300 seconds, leaving MISO tri-stated and loading Z into ISRAM.
soc_timer0_boot_runtime.observed_corrected_path: No-override run: PoweredUp=1; READ opcode 0x03 decoded; SPI MISO drives data; first RXFIFO APB response is 0xb7100040; bootloader writes 0x400010b7 to ISRAM; Timer0 MMIO/readback and counting pass; DSRAM[0] commits 1; PC parks at 0x00010028.

monitor_exact_join_followup.checks: All checks pass, including exact one-to-one LSU/AXI/APB UART write match; address 0x40002000, data 0x00000055, strobes 1111, ordered timestamps.
monitor_exact_join_followup.limitations: Uses a deterministic structural monitor stub, not the real SoC/Stage1 firmware path.

step4_checker_selfproof.limitations: Uses step4_apb_bridge_model, not the real axi_lite_to_apb or SoC. XSim ignores cover property statements.
